title: Multiplicativity of the inner-product sign under coordinatewise XOR
statement:
Fix $n \in \bbn$, and for $u,v \in \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$ write $\langle u, v\rangle \in \mathrm{Bool}$ for the mod-$2$ inner product, and $s(b) \in \{\pm 1\}$ for the Boolean sign of $b$ (so $s(\mathrm{false}) = 1$ and $s(\mathrm{true}) = -1$). Then for all $x, y, z \in \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$,
\[
  s\big(\langle x, y\rangle\big)\cdot s\big(\langle x, z\rangle\big)
  = s\big(\langle x,\, y \oplus z\rangle\big),
\]
where $y \oplus z$ denotes the coordinatewise XOR of $y$ and $z$.
hypotheses_covered: x, y, z arbitrary n-bit Boolean inputs
replaced:
For all $x, y, z : \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$,
\[
  \mathrm{boolSign}(\mathrm{IP}(x, y)) \cdot \mathrm{boolSign}(\mathrm{IP}(x, z))
  = \mathrm{boolSign}(\mathrm{IP}(x,\, y \oplus z)).
\]
The Walsh character for the inner product is multiplicative in its second argument
under coordinatewise XOR.
